industry.structure: Global card payments is a concentrated oligopoly among Visa, Mastercard, American Express, and large bank issuers. Closed-loop issuers like Amex capture both network and lending economics; open-loop networks earn processing fees with less balance-sheet risk.
industry.share_shift: Amex gains share when premium consumer and small-business spend grows and when merchants accept higher discount rates for affluent cardmembers. Fintech wallets and bank co-brands compete on rewards; Amex differentiates on service and fee-based card revenue.
industry.trend: Net card fee growth, B2B payments digitization, and international billed business are live industry tailwinds; credit provisions and funding costs are the main cyclical headwinds for issuer-network models.
